name: Main Entrance
note: North side of the festival grounds, reached over the vehicle bridge at the main entrance to Town Park.

name: Merch Store
note: North side of the grounds, next to the Main Entrance and the House of Brews Bar.

name: House of Brews Bar
note: North side of the grounds, next to the Merch Store and Main Entrance. Up to ten rotating styles per day; each style is featured on only one day and in limited quantity.

name: Main Stage
note: The current stage was unveiled in 2016, replacing the Fred Shellman Memorial Stage built by the Town of Telluride in 1991.

name: Music Maker Drink House
note: Original artwork, vinyl listening stations and artist meet-and-greets.

name: Sound Booth & ADA Viewing
note: Out in the crowd facing the Main Stage. The designated wheelchair space is directly in front of it, and high-back chairs are not permitted between the sound booth and the stage.

name: Beer Garden
note: Between the Main Stage and the Blues Stage. Home of the four Brewers Showcase tasting sessions.

name: Free Drinking Water
note: Free drinking water is available on the grounds — bring your own bottle.

name: Food & Craft Vendors
note: Food and craft vendors on the grounds; individual vendor names are not published by the festival.

name: Port-a-Potties & Hand Sinks
note: Port-a-potties, hand sinks, and trash / recycling / compost stations. Handicap porta-potties are available.

name: Camp Pale Ale Beer Lounge
note: Sierra Nevada's bar, also referenced as the High Altitude Craft Beer Lounge. Six rare specialty beers plus a festival-only flavor; rare beers are announced from the stage between sets each day and poured until the keg is dry.

name: Truck Stage
note: Presented by Sierra Nevada; referenced on one artist page as an "Artist Pop-Up — Festival Field." Its exact position on the grounds is NOT published — this pin is provisional.

name: Blues Stage
note: Introduced in 2015 and indoors, inside the Town Park Hanley Pavilion. Theater-style seating and a full bar with beer, wine and cocktails. Doubles as the largest Juke Joint venue at night.

name: Rainbow Kids Area
note: Back northeast section of the grounds. Ages 3 and up. Climbing wall, inflatable bounce games, face painting, a talent show, workshops, and parades on Saturday and Sunday. Fees are charged for the games; prices and hours are not published.

name: Medical Tent
note: East edge of the festival grounds, campground side. EMTs carry basics like ibuprofen and sunblock.

name: Shade Alley
note: The back perimeter of the grounds — the only place sunshade tents are permitted.

name: Main Campground
note: 5-Day Camping, $80. Large wooded area east of the festival grounds, open Wednesday–Monday, backing onto Bear Creek Wilderness. Charcoal and propane both permitted.

name: Campground Stage
note: A handcrafted wooden stage built by a local artisan from wood taken from a nearby river, set among the trees by the river in the Town Park Campground. Sets are billed as Campground Sessions.

name: Zone 1 Camping
note: 5-Day Camping, $80. Smaller wooded section in the southeast corner of the Main Campground, adjacent to Bear Creek Wilderness. Open Wednesday–Monday.

name: Warner Field Camping
note: 4-Day Camping, $70. At the baseball field entrance to Town Park, treeless and directly adjacent to the Beer Garden and Tasting Sessions. Open Thursday–Monday. Propane grills and BBQs allowed; charcoal prohibited.

name: Town Park Parking Lot (limited ADA parking)
note: Limited handicap parking, reached over the vehicle bridge at the main entrance to the Park. There is no general festival parking lot.

name: Warming Hut — Lost & Found
note: Next to the Town Park Oval, on the path from the Box Office to the main entrance.

name: Festival Box Office
note: 300 E Pacific Street. Wristband pickup: bring your Front Gate digital ticket and valid photo ID in person. Thu 10:00–18:30 · Fri & Sat 09:00–20:15 · Sun 10:00–19:15.

name: Information Station
note: At the entrance to town. Camping, parking and ticket questions. Open 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM Thursday through Saturday.

name: Elks Park
note: Site of the Blisters & Brews 5K (Saturday 8:50–9:30 AM) and the free Yoga Sessions (Saturday and Sunday 10:00–11:00 AM).

name: Liz
note: Juke Joint venue hosting the stand-up comedy bill on both Juke Joint nights. The festival publishes only the name "Liz" — no full venue name or address.

name: Sheridan Opera House
note: Historic Telluride theater. Hosts Thursday's Bal De Maison opening show, Juke Joints on Friday and Saturday, and Sunday's Fais Do-Do closing show.

name: The Moon at O'Bannon's
note: Intimate in-town room, Juke Joint venue on Friday and Saturday.

name: Elks Lodge
note: 472 West Pacific Avenue (address per Visit Telluride, not the festival site). Juke Joint venue, and the site of Blues For Breakfast and the Telluride Blues Challenge.

name: Gondola — Telluride Station
note: Oak Street, at the west end of the commercial core — the opposite end of town from Town Park. Free. Festival-week hours: Thu 6:30 AM–12:00 AM · Fri & Sat 6:30 AM–2:00 AM · Sun 6:30 AM–12:00 AM.

name: Galloping Goose Shuttle
note: Free town shuttle running fixed laps every 20 minutes, 7:00 AM–midnight during the concert weekend. Stops every few blocks, marked by signs.

name: SilverJack Parking Garage
note: 155 W Pacific Avenue. $2.00/hour plus a $50/night overnight fee.

name: Madeline Hotel & Residences
note: In Mountain Village, reached by the free gondola. Hosts Thursday's Beer Pairing Dinner and a Sunday Blues For Breakfast location.
